title: Vanilla-Glazed Yeast-Raised Doughnuts
summary: Light, airy yeast-raised ring doughnuts fried to a golden band and dipped in a thin vanilla glaze that sets glossy.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook (or large bowl)
8 cm round cutter and 2.5 cm cutter (or a doughnut cutter)
2 baking trays lined with oiled baking paper
large heavy pan or casserole, at least 24 cm wide
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Combine the flour, sugar, yeast, salt and nutmeg, then add the warm milk, egg and vanilla and knead on medium-low (or by hand) for 5 min. Add the soft butter a little at a time and keep kneading 6-8 min more until the dough is smooth, stretchy and just a little tacky. Adding butter after the gluten has formed keeps the doughnuts tender without weakening their structure.

steps.title: Let it rise
steps.text: Cover the bowl and leave it somewhere warm for 1-1.5 h. It should roughly double in size.

steps.title: Roll and cut rings
steps.text: Press the air out and roll the dough 1.2 cm thick on a floured worktop. Stamp out 8 cm rounds and cut a 2.5 cm hole from the middle of each, re-rolling the scraps once to make 12 rings. Lay them on the oiled paper with space between them.

steps.title: Prove until puffy
steps.text: Cover loosely and leave for 30-45 min. When pressed gently with a fingertip, the dough should spring back slowly and leave a slight dent; under-proved rings fry dense, over-proved ones collapse.

steps.title: Heat the oil safely
steps.text: Pour oil into the heavy pan to a depth of about 4 cm, keeping it no more than half full, and heat it to 175 °C on the thermometer. Steady temperature is the key to a dry, golden doughnut rather than a greasy one.

steps.title: Fry in small batches
steps.text: Slide in 3 rings at a time and fry 60-90 seconds on each side, holding the oil between 170 and 180 °C. Lift them out when deep golden with a pale ring round the middle and about 90 °C at the centre, then drain on the rack.

steps.title: Glaze while warm
steps.text: Whisk the icing sugar, hot water and vanilla to a smooth, pourable glaze. Dip the top of each warm doughnut, let the excess run off and leave them on the rack for 10 min. Warmth thins the glaze so it sets in a sheer, crackly layer.

tips: The biggest mistake is frying in oil that is too cool; below 170 °C the doughnuts soak up fat, so check the thermometer between batches.
Use a heavy, wide pan and never fill it more than half full with oil.
If the glaze is too thick to drip, whisk in hot water a teaspoon at a time.
Fry the cut-out holes too; they take about 30 seconds a side.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten the day they are made. Keep any leftovers loosely covered at room temperature for up to 1 day; freezing is not recommended once glazed.
